spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A nonnegative trigonometric polynomial packages many shifted logarithmic-derivative inequalities into one positive combination. Its coefficient geometry, especially b0, b1, and the total b, becomes direct leverage on the eventual zero-free constant.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines PK(x)=∑_{k=0}^K b_k cos(kx) with b_k≥0, b1>b0, and PK(x)≥0 for all real x. It recalls degree-4 and degree-5 choices from Ford and Nielsen, then records coefficient aggregates for new degree-40 and degree-46 polynomials used in two main theorems, with full tables and search details deferred to Section 8.
directed.conceptual_reading: Positivity converts a weighted sum of oscillatory prime terms into a one-sided inequality. The auxiliary polynomial is therefore part of the proof certificate, while its coefficients expose a finite-dimensional design problem embedded in the analytic argument.
directed.representation_or_bridge: PK(t log n) bridges trigonometric nonnegativity to nonnegativity of a mollified prime sum; the aggregates b0,b1,b summarize the aspects later inequalities consume.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Admissibility is global in x and cannot be inferred from favorable aggregate coefficients alone. The listed polynomials are constructed candidates, not established optima, and their tables occur outside this unit.
directed.uncertainty: The constraints and roles are prose-stable; exact coefficient decimals and factorizations should be checked against the source tables.
